Render cleaning, because the finish is thinner than it looks

Acrylic, sand, texture coat and bagged render across Melbourne. The decorative face of a rendered wall is a couple of millimetres thick and a pressure washer removes it in a single pass. Render is always soft washed, and the marks that will not come off are usually telling you something about the wall rather than the dirt.

  • Never pressure cleaned
  • Treated, then rinsed top down
  • Failing render reported, not washed over
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. House and building washing
  4. Render cleaning

What render actually is

A thin decorative coat over something structural: blockwork, brick, or a polystyrene panel. The part you see is usually two to five millimetres thick, and in acrylic renders the texture comes from aggregate held in a polymer binder that sits right at the surface.

That is why pressure is wrong here in a way it is not wrong on concrete. There is no depth to work into. A pressure washer does not clean the top layer of an acrylic render, it removes it, leaving a lighter patch with a different texture that will never weather back to match. Those patches are the most common permanent exterior damage we are asked to look at, and nothing fixes them except rerendering the elevation.

By render type

Four finishes, four behaviours

Most Melbourne homes built since the nineties have one of these. If yours is older it may be a cement render, which is tougher but usually has other problems.

How each type behaves and what it tells you when it will not come clean.
  Character How it is cleaned What a permanent mark usually means
Acrylic texture Polymer binder with aggregate, flexible, most common on newer builds Soft wash, moderate dwell, rinsed before it dries The binder has been stripped by pressure, or UV has chalked the surface
Sand finish Fine sand in the top coat, often over blockwork Soft wash, gentle rinse so the sand face is not disturbed The sand face has gone, which shows as a smoother, darker patch
Bagged brick A thin slurry coat rubbed over brickwork Lowest pressure, longer dwell, tested first The coat has worn through and the brick below is showing
Cement render Traditional sand and cement, hard and rigid Soft wash, and the wall checked for cracking first Carbonation or a crack letting water move through the wall

Swipe for the rest of the columns

What the marks tell you

Not all of it is dirt

Spotting from the eaves down

Mould. It starts where the wall stays shaded and damp longest and spreads downward. Comes off entirely once it is treated rather than rinsed.

A green band near the ground

Algae, fed by splash back off the path and by moisture wicking up. Clean it, and then look at whether the ground level sits too high against the wall.

Streaks below a window or a join

Water tracking the same path every time it rains. Cleaning removes the stain. If the flashing or the sill is the cause it will come back in the same shape.

A chalky film on your hand

The binder breaking down under UV. Washing will not fix it and heavy cleaning makes it worse. It is a repaint, and we will tell you.

A patch lighter than everything around it

Previous pressure damage. Permanent. We will not pretend otherwise or try to blend it by cleaning harder.

Cracking with staining around it

Water is getting into the wall. That is a render repair before it is a cleaning job, and washing it first just tells you where.

If the render is failing, we will say so before we start

Drummy sections, cracking with staining, visible chalking or a face that has already been stripped are wall problems, not dirt. Cleaning them does not help and in some cases makes them worse. You get told at quote stage rather than after a day on site, and nobody is charged to find out.

  • 2 to 5 mmTypical thickness of the decorative face on an acrylic render. There is no depth to clean into.
  • 3 to 5 yearsHow long a properly treated render elevation stays clean in Melbourne, against under a year if it is only rinsed.
  • South and south-eastThe elevations that go first, every time, because they never dry out through winter.
  • No laddersSoft washing a two storey render wall is done from the ground, so nothing leans against the finish.

Questions

Asked about rendered walls

Why can render not be pressure cleaned?

Because pressure takes the texture off the render along with the dirt, and it leaves a permanently lighter patch wherever the wand lingered. There is no way to fix that except taking the rest of the wall down to match.

Soft washing against pressure cleaning explains what each method actually does.

Can you pressure clean render?

No, and this is the clearest case of it on a house. A pressure washer removes the decorative face of an acrylic or sand render rather than cleaning it, and the lighter, smoother patch it leaves is permanent. Rerendering the elevation is the only fix.

Render is soft washed, every time, with the solution doing the work.

How long does render cleaning last?

Three to five years on a reasonably exposed wall. Less on a south-facing elevation under trees, because the conditions keep favouring the growth.

If it comes back within a year, the wall was rinsed rather than treated. The difference is invisible on the day and obvious eighteen months later.

There are streaks under my windows that will not come off. Why?

Because they are usually not dirt. Water running the same path off a sill or a failed flashing leaves a mineral track in the render. Cleaning lifts the biological part and the track stays faintly visible, and it will darken again in the same shape next winter.

The fix is the flashing or the sill drip edge, which is a builder's job. We will point out where it is coming from.

My render looks chalky and leaves powder on my hand. Can you clean that?

No, and heavy cleaning makes it worse. Chalking is the binder in the render breaking down under UV, so what is on your hand is the surface itself. A gentle wash will remove the growth sitting on it, but the wall will still look flat and faded.

That is a repaint or a recoat. We will tell you at quote stage rather than after.

Will the mould come back if the wall is in permanent shade?

Sooner than on a sunny elevation, yes, because the conditions have not changed. Treating it properly still buys years rather than months.

Two things genuinely help: cutting back whatever is holding the shade and the moisture, and making sure ground level and garden beds are not sitting against the render. Both do more than cleaning more often does.

Do you clean the eaves and gutters at the same time?

The eaves, fascia and the outside of the gutters are part of a render or house wash as standard, because they are the dirtiest part of the elevation and washing the wall under a dirty eave is pointless.

Clearing the inside of the gutters is a different job and is quoted separately. Gutter cleaning.
